candidate.title: PIP-Seq
candidate.scope: Protein interaction profile sequencing (PIP-Seq), restricted to the assigned poster row beginning with formaldehyde-crosslinked RNA-protein complexes. Both dsRNase and ssRNase paths and their respective protein-depleted RNase-insensitivity controls are targets of this single workflow. The initial summary icon is descriptive; AGO-CLIP above, hiCLIP below, and the chemical structure at right are neighboring context. UV and noncrosslinked preparations described in the literature are outside this depicted implementation. The poster draws size selection, DSN normalization, then a combined library-preparation/sequencing caption. The primary-paper-supported graph explicitly separates that final caption into library construction, DSN normalization of the prepared library, and sequencing; the literal poster order is retained in branch-specific corrections.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations belong to the single depicted formaldehyde-crosslinked PIP-Seq implementation. The two nuclease groups each contain a protein-present footprint track and a Proteinase-before-RNase control track. Shared downstream captions apply as separate local instances on each of the four retained arrows; the primary paper explicitly reports four libraries. The initial crosslinked complex is an input state. No adjacent method, unshown UV/noncrosslinked preparation, nuclear-isolation adaptation, or named library kit is added as a target. Protein-protected sites are inferred from sequence enrichment over the same-nuclease control; surviving RNA alone does not prove protection, identify a particular protein, or establish a single direct protein-RNA contact. Formaldehyde can retain indirect associations. Branch-specific corrections resolve the poster’s compressed DSN/library-preparation order using the primary implementation. The supplied plant-structure review further cautions that small bulges/loops may evade nuclease resolution and adjacent formaldehyde-linked proteins may produce a single extended protected region; this is secondary evidence about interpretation, not a new workflow.
